**Answer: $Q_{LV}(B_N) = N$ for all $N \ge 2$.**

This relies on the Copeland–Pommersheim characterization, which I recalled from memory rather than checked against the paper. It says that for symmetric oracle identification, Las Vegas (zero-error) query complexity is the least $t$ such that every irreducible representation of $G$ appears in the $t$-fold tensor power of the permutation representation $\mathbb{C}[X]^{\otimes t}$.

**Setup.** The natural action of $B_N$ is on the $2N$ signed basis vectors $X=\{\pm e_1,\dots,\pm e_N\}$. Irreps of $B_N$ are labelled by bipartitions $(\lambda,\mu)$ with $|\lambda|+|\mu|=N$.

**Orbits on $X^t$.** A $t$-tuple of signed basis vectors uses $k\le\min(t,N)$ distinct coordinates. Its stabilizer is $B_{N-k}$, acting on the unused coordinates. So $\mathbb{C}[X]^{\otimes t}$ is a sum of copies of $\mathrm{Ind}_{B_{N-k}}^{B_N}\mathbf{1}$ for $k\le\min(t,N)$.

**Constituents.** Since $\mathrm{Ind}_{B_{N-k}}^{B_N}\mathbf{1}$ contains $\mathrm{Ind}_{B_{N-k}\times B_k}^{B_N}(\mathbf{1}\otimes\rho)$ for every $\rho\in\mathrm{Irr}(B_k)$, the Littlewood–Richardson rule for hyperoctahedral groups gives: $(\lambda,\mu)$ appears at level $t$ iff there is $k\le\min(t,N)$ with $\mu\subseteq$ a suitable $\beta$ of size $k-|\alpha|$ and $\lambda/\alpha$ a horizontal strip of size $N-k$. The largest horizontal strip removable from $\lambda$ has size $\lambda_1$, so the condition becomes $k\ge N-\lambda_1$ and $k\ge|\mu|$.

Hence the minimal level at which $(\lambda,\mu)$ appears is
$$t(\lambda,\mu)=\max(N-\lambda_1,\ |\mu|).$$

**Maximizing.** The maximum over all bipartitions of $N$ is attained at $(\lambda,\mu)=(\varnothing,(N))$, where $t=N$. This is the one-dimensional character $\prod(\text{signs})$, which first appears only at level $N$.

**Check at $N=2$.** $B_2$ is the dihedral group of order 8 acting on the four vertices of a square. A single copy of the permutation representation misses two of the four one-dimensional irreps. At $t=2$, the orbit of adjacent vertex pairs has trivial stabilizer, so the induced representation is the regular representation and contains everything. This gives $Q_{LV}(B_2)=2$, matching the formula.

ANSWER: $N$
